1.explanation: The root of this accessibility issue lies in the Toggle component’s render method. In Toggle.js, inside the <label>, both <span> elements that hold the labelA (Off) and labelB (On) values are rendered with aria-hidden="true". That attribute explicitly hides them from screen readers, so VoiceOver never speaks them. To fix this, the render method in Toggle should be updated to remove (or conditionally omit) aria-hidden on these text spans or provide an appropriate aria-label or aria--labelledby on the input. Adjusting Toggle.render is therefore the key place to remove the unwanted aria-hidden attribute and ensure the labels are announced.
1.bug_scenario: When keyboard-navigating to the Toggle component and activating it, VoiceOver does not announce the “On” or “Off” labels. In the DOM you can see that both the left and right label spans are stamped with aria-hidden="true", preventing the assistive technology from reading them.

2.explanation: The bug stems from the Toggle component’s render() method in Toggle.js, where the two <span> elements that show the "Off" (labelA) and "On" (labelB) text are explicitly marked aria-hidden="true". This hides those labels from screen readers such as VoiceOver, so no announcement is made when toggling. Removing or adjusting the aria-hidden attribute (or moving the labels into an aria-label or aria-labelledby construct on the input) in the render() method of Toggle is the key fix point.
2.bug_scenario: When using the default Carbon React Toggle component with VoiceOver on macOS, the screen reader does not announce the "Off" and "On" labels as you toggle. Inspecting the markup shows that the two <span> elements that display those labels have aria-hidden="true", so their contents are hidden from assistive technology.
